title: The Q2 2026 Report Card: Who Won, Who Lost, and Why | The Weekly Wrap
summary: Eisman reviews a technology-led second-quarter rally already showing signs of reversal. He favors scarce semiconductor and power capacity over capital-hungry model builders, questions weak consulting and consumer turnarounds, and discusses financial-sector leadership. He criticizes Greenspan's regulatory legacy and argues that greater US economic dynamism favors US investments over Europe.
assessment: Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts the episode; guest turns are inferred from introductions and conversational context.
framework_points: Look inside sector returns to distinguish scarce suppliers from the buyers funding their growth.
Capital intensity requires durable competitive protection to generate acceptable returns.
Separate social-policy preferences from investment-return judgments.
tools_and_charts: S&P 500, Nasdaq and eleven sector returns through June 24
Micron earnings, forward P/E and supply outlook
Capital raising and business-model comparison for hyperscalers
transcript_cautions: Quarter review is explicitly an incomplete-quarter snapshot, not final June 30 performance.
Micron EPS is rendered $251; primary disclosure is $25.11, so the caption numeral is unreliable.
Captions render moat as moes and MOU as anou.
Greenspan is repeatedly said to have retired in 2005; Federal Reserve history says January 31, 2006.
